issue: Is a fact that only increases the maximum sentence, such as a 'death results' allegation, an element of the offense of conviction for purposes of the statutory elements and divisibility analysis?
provision: 18 U.S.C. § 1962(d); Sixth Amendment jury-trial right (Apprendi v. New Jersey, 530 U.S. 466 (2000))

sides.position: A fact relevant only to an enhanced statutory penalty, such as 'death results,' is an element of the crime of conviction, so the statute is divisible by that fact.
cases: United States v. Tsarnaev, 968 F.3d 24 (1st Cir. 2020)

sides.position: An 'element' relevant only to an enhanced sentence is not necessarily an element of the crime of conviction; Apprendi's 'element' language rests on the Sixth Amendment jury-trial guarantee and does not define the range of criminal conduct.
cases: United States v. Antonio Simmons, 999 F.3d 199 (4th Cir. 2021)

this_court: Fourth Circuit's position: an element relevant only to an enhanced sentence is not necessarily an element of the crime of conviction. The court rejects the First Circuit's contrary premise.
quote: We disagree with the First Circuit’s premise that an “element” relevant only to an enhanced sentence is necessarily an element of the crime of conviction.
cite: United States v. Antonio Simmons, 999 F.3d 199 (4th Cir. 2021)
